I discovered that you can install Linux Mint using a program tool "Rufus" on an USB drive. So I got a 256 GB USB flash drive that is intended to be booted from. The plan is that it contains the complete Linux that I can pull from the PC when I start up Windows. And Linux becomes my main OS from now on.

Now I have an existing Linux Mint on my Windows and is used in a VM ware.

Concerns I have is this:

* Migrating my current Linux in VMware version to the USB without having to reinstall or configure anything.. * If possible to keep the VMWare Linux synchronized with the USB version. Sometimes I need to have both Windows and Linux running at the same time. * A way to backup and restore the USB image to my NAS drive in case it crashes. * Locking Windows completely out from that USB drive so it can't access any bit from that USB even when it is still plugged into the computer. * Unclear is how reliable the USB flash drive is when I use it as a normal hard disk.

In the future I tend to migrate from the flash drive to a real hard disk and from then on contain Windows inside a VM machine so I can cut it off completely from the Internet when I want to.

Edit: I used USB drive but it is a USB Flash drive

Edit2: Massive failure, I can boot from the USB flash drive and do get into the Linux startup where I can click on the install icon and then scripts error and the install fails. So back to the VM version on Windows.
Doing the next phase. Install Linux Mint on an external USB drive

Migrating my current Linux in VMware version to the USB without having to reinstall or configure anything..

If you install the OS to a new disk, of course you'll have to also reinstall any needed programs which aren't bundled with the OS. You can create a new account with the same user name on the newly installed OS, and then copy your home folder from the old installation.

You might instead try booting a live disk and copying the entire filesystem from the old disk to the new disk. That way you won't have to install or configure anything, assuming it works. I don't recommend this because it takes so long and is somewhat more risky, but that's for you to judge.

A way to backup and restore the USB image to my NAS drive in case it crashes.

I'm currently using an extremely simple shell script and root crontab entry. My configuration is somewhat unconventional for GNU/Linux systems, so you'd probably be better served by these pages:

  • http://www.mikerubel.org/computers/rsync_snapshots/
  • https://wiki.archlinux.org/index.php/rsync

Locking Windows completely out from that USB drive so it can't access any bit from that USB even when it is still plugged into the computer.
